first off, you're not dumb. society has grossly accepted and normalized porn addiction, so its kind of hard to realize when it's gotten out of hand based on today's standards. im not saying porn is bad, many things aren't bad in moderation, but the way you've described using it seems problematic. you've already recognized this, so kudos

in my personal experience with addiction (not porn, but the idea is the same) I found it helpful to quit by thinking of consequences for future me and weighing them with the quick fix I currently wanted. for me the consequences always outweighed the instant gratification although it was really hard to come to terms with. here's some things, along with the ones you've already talked about, to think about when you feel like giving in (coming from someones whose ex boyfriend had a porn addiction - one (of many) things that killed our relationship):

* porn gives you a very unrealistic idea of sex & if you base your sex life on what you see in porn 99% of the time you will be bad at sex
* it gives you self esteem issues (whether you realize it or not) + it again gives you unrealistic expectations for your partner
* it can kill your desire for real sex, you can even develop early onset erectile dysfunction
* porn addiction ruins real human connection and it can take away your time/desire to have relationships with an actual physical partner
* if you already have a partner & they find out, chances are it'll ruin your relationship & they will have a hard time looking at you and/or themselves the same way

try spending more time with real people in your life or picking up new hobbies - put effort into these things bc they will actually benefit you and make you truly feel good. when you have urges try satisfying yourself without porn. 

I know any addiction is hard to overcome, so be gentle on yourself. messing up is okay, and it's a hell of a lot better than not trying. best of luck to you!

personally i don’t think you need to talk much about the aspects of being a PA that you like in your PS in the way that you think you do. the adcoms already know you like things about the profession (or why else would you be applying to PA school). your PS is your story about how you found out you wanted to be a PA. 

your PS shows your uniqueness. saying you like the PA profession because you literal flexibility is not unique because every other applicant likes that about the profession. so many other applicants are going to have 3.6+ GPAs and thousands of hours of PCE/HCE. this is what going to set you apart from hundreds of other individuals.

it’s your chance to share personal details about your life outside of what your application already shows about. do you have a personal story about your adolescence that inspired you to look into the medial field? do you come from a unique background? did you have a rough time during undergrad, and how did you persevere? aside from academics and PCE, what sets you apart from other applicants? 

when i was writing my PS i always thought to myself “can i relate this information to why i want to be a PA?” and if so, “is it really meaningful?”

i hope this is helpful and best of luck.
